meta.title: Best Laptop Under ₹30,000 in India (2026): Real Picks for Students and First-Time Buyers
meta.description: We ranked the best laptops under ₹30,000 in India for 2026 — real CPU, RAM, SSD and battery comparisons, plus one popular model to skip.
meta.short_desc: Five usable laptops for students and first-time buyers — and one to avoid.

headings.text: What actually matters in a laptop under ₹30,000

cta.headline: Buy for the SSD and RAM, not the brand
cta.sub: Compare current sale prices on Amazon, Flipkart and brand stores. Student discounts and bank offers move weekly.

faq.q: Is a laptop under ₹30,000 worth buying in 2026?
faq.a: Yes, for students, online classes, office work, and browsing. Skip gaming and video editing at this budget — those need ₹50,000+. Look for at least 8GB RAM, an SSD (not HDD), and a current-gen Intel i3 or AMD Ryzen 3.

faq.q: What RAM is enough at this price?
faq.a: 8GB is the minimum for Windows 11. 4GB laptops exist but they crawl when Chrome has 5+ tabs open. If a 4GB model is on sale, verify it has an empty RAM slot to upgrade later.

faq.q: SSD vs HDD — does it really matter?
faq.a: Massively. A 256GB SSD laptop boots in 12-15 seconds; a 1TB HDD laptop takes 60-90 seconds. App launch and file copy are 3-5x faster on SSD. Never buy an HDD-only laptop in 2026.

faq.q: Intel i3 vs AMD Ryzen 3 at ₹30,000?
faq.a: AMD Ryzen 3 wins on multi-core performance and battery life at this budget. Intel i3 (12th/13th gen) wins on single-core responsiveness and software compatibility. For students and office work, both are fine.

faq.q: How long should the battery last?
faq.a: 6-8 hours of real use is the realistic floor for studying on campus. Anything below 5 hours means carrying the charger everywhere. Marketing claims of 10+ hours usually mean 6-7 in real use.

meta.tldr_pick: The Acer Aspire 3 (Ryzen 3 7320U, 8GB, 512GB SSD) is the best laptop under ₹30,000 in India — current AMD Ryzen 3, fast SSD, 8GB DDR5 RAM, and an honest 7-hour battery. Buy it at around ₹26,990 during sales on Amazon.
key_takeaways: SSD is non-negotiable: never buy an HDD-only laptop in 2026 — boot and app launch times will frustrate you daily.
8GB RAM is the floor: 4GB laptops exist but struggle with Windows 11 and modern browsers.
Skip the HP 15s with 1TB HDD: it looks attractive at the price but the HDD makes it painful to use.
AMD Ryzen 3 7320U / 7430U wins on battery life over Intel i3 at this price.
meta.who_for: Students (engineering, commerce, school) buying a first laptop, parents shopping for a child's online-class machine, and anyone who needs a working Windows laptop for browsing, MS Office and light work without paying ₹40,000+. This guide ranks the 5 best laptops under ₹30,000 for Indian buyers in 2026.
meta.methodology: We compared 8 laptops between ₹22,000 and ₹30,000 available on Amazon India, Flipkart and brand stores in 2026. For each, we evaluated CPU generation, RAM type and capacity, storage type (SSD vs HDD), battery life in real use, build quality, keyboard and trackpad, and warranty support. Picks were validated against manufacturer specs, current sale pricing, and verified buyer reviews. This guide was first published in August 2026 and is reviewed every 60 days.

body:
What actually matters in a laptop under ₹30,000

The best laptop under ₹30,000 in 2026 is not the one with the biggest screen or the loudest spec sheet. It is the one that boots in 15 seconds, opens Chrome quickly, and lasts 6+ hours on battery during a college day. Skip the marketing claims and focus on CPU (Ryzen 3 7000-series or Intel i3 12th gen+), RAM (8GB minimum), storage (SSD, not HDD), and battery (real 6+ hours).

Two hardware decisions dominate this segment. First, an SSD or HDD: an SSD makes the laptop feel 3-5x faster in daily use. A 1TB HDD laptop looks attractive on the spec sheet, but every boot, every app launch, every file copy will test your patience. Second, the CPU generation: a Ryzen 3 7320U is meaningfully faster and more efficient than a Ryzen 3 5300U, and an i3-1215U is faster than an i3-1115G4. The 2-generation gap matters.

Under ₹30,000 you will not get a dedicated GPU, a 16GB RAM option, or a 1TB SSD. Accept that — and instead pick a laptop that does the basics well. The picks below are the models we would buy for our own siblings starting college in 2026.

If you only buy one thing from this list: get the Acer Aspire 3 with the Ryzen 3 7320U, 8GB DDR5 and 512GB SSD. It is the most balanced under ₹30,000 — current AMD silicon, fast DDR5 RAM, roomy SSD, and a battery that genuinely lasts a college day.

The 2026 sweet spot — what to look for

At this budget the right spec sheet in 2026 is: AMD Ryzen 3 7320U / 7430U OR Intel i3-1215U / i3-1305U, 8GB DDR4 or DDR5, 256GB or 512GB SSD, 15.6-inch Full HD display (1920x1080). Anything older than a 12th-gen Intel or a 5000-series AMD Ryzen is dated. Anything with 4GB RAM is too slow for Windows 11. Anything with an HDD is too slow for daily use.

RAM — 8GB is the floor

4GB laptops exist at this budget. They will boot Windows 11 and run one or two apps. As soon as you open Chrome with five tabs, MS Word, and Zoom, they crawl. Buy 8GB minimum. If a 4GB model is heavily discounted, check if it has an empty SO-DIMM slot for a later upgrade — most do.

Display — FHD is non-negotiable

1366x768 (HD) displays are still on the market in 2026 at this price. They look pixelated for text, and most apps assume a 1920x1080 panel. Spend the extra ₹2,000-₹4,000 for a Full HD display. Your eyes will thank you during 6-hour study sessions.

Battery — marketing vs real use

Brands quote 8-12 hours. Real use with Wi-Fi, Chrome and 50% brightness is closer to 5-7 hours. AMD Ryzen laptops consistently beat Intel i3 on battery in this segment by 1-1.5 hours. If battery is critical for campus life, prefer Ryzen.

Our top 5 picks

⭐ Top Pick

1. Acer Aspire 3 (Ryzen 3 7320U, 8GB DDR5, 512GB SSD)

Usually ₹26,990–₹29,490
CPURyzen 3 7320U (4C/8T)
RAM8GB DDR5
Storage512GB SSD
Display15.6" FHD

The Aspire 3 with the Ryzen 3 7320U is the most balanced laptop under ₹30,000 in 2026. The 7320U is current AMD silicon with 4 cores / 8 threads, more than enough for online classes, MS Office, browsing with 15+ Chrome tabs, and light photo editing. 8GB of DDR5 RAM is future-proofed, and the 512GB SSD gives you room to install apps without immediately running out of space.

Battery is the strong suit: expect 6.5-7.5 hours of real use. The display is a 1080p TN panel — not as colour-accurate as IPS, but acceptable for study and browsing. Build quality is plastic but does not creak. Acer's service network is solid in metros and decent in tier-2 cities.

✓ What works

  • Current-gen Ryzen 3 7320U
  • DDR5 RAM at this price (rare)
  • 512GB SSD room
  • 7-hour real battery life
  • Full HD display

✗ Trade-offs

  • TN display (limited viewing angles)
  • Plastic build
  • No backlit keyboard on most variants

🥈 Best Intel Pick

2. Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 (i3-1215U, 8GB, 512GB SSD)

Usually ₹28,490–₹30,990
CPUIntel i3-1215U (6C/8T)
RAM8GB DDR4
Storage512GB SSD
Display15.6" FHD IPS

The IdeaPad Slim 3 with the i3-1215U is the best Intel option in this bracket. The 12th-gen i3 has 6 cores / 8 threads — generous for the price — and the IPS display has better viewing angles than the Acer's TN panel. Lenovo's build quality is a step above Acer at the same price: the keyboard is firmer, the trackpad is more reliable, and the hinge is tested for 25,000 open/close cycles.

Battery is shorter than the AMD Acer: expect 5.5-6.5 hours of real use. If your day is mostly at a desk with the charger nearby, this is fine. If you need to be unplugged for 7+ hours, prefer the Acer or ASUS.

✓ What works

  • 12th-gen Intel i3 with 6 cores
  • IPS Full HD display
  • Sturdy Lenovo build
  • Reliable keyboard and trackpad

✗ Trade-offs

  • Battery is 1 hour shorter than AMD rivals
  • Often ₹1,500-₹2,500 more than the Acer
  • DDR4 RAM, not DDR5

💰 Best Display + Specs Combo

3. ASUS VivoBook 15 (Ryzen 3 7320U, 8GB DDR5, 512GB SSD)

Usually ₹27,490–₹29,990
CPURyzen 3 7320U (4C/8T)
RAM8GB DDR5
Storage512GB SSD
Display15.6" FHD

The VivoBook 15 with the Ryzen 3 7320U is the direct competitor to the Acer Aspire 3 — same CPU, same DDR5 RAM, same 512GB SSD. The differences are small: ASUS uses a slightly nicer chassis finish, has a fingerprint reader on most variants, and ships with a more useful pre-installed software bundle. The display is the same TN-grade as the Acer.

Battery life is 6-7 hours of real use — comparable to the Acer. ASUS service is solid in metros but spottier in smaller cities. If the price is the same as the Acer, this is a slightly nicer pick. If the Acer is ₹1,000-₹1,500 cheaper, prefer the Acer for value.

  • DDR5 RAM
  • Fingerprint reader
  • Slightly nicer build finish

✗ Trade-offs

  • TN display (same as Acer)
  • Often costs ₹500-₹1,500 more than Acer
  • Service network spottier in tier-2 cities

4. HP 15s (Ryzen 3 5300U, 8GB DDR4, 512GB SSD)

Usually ₹29,490–₹31,990
CPURyzen 3 5300U (4C/8T)
RAM8GB DDR4
Storage512GB SSD
Display15.6" FHD IPS

The HP 15s with the Ryzen 3 5300U is one generation behind the Acer and ASUS picks, but it has two advantages: an IPS display (better viewing angles) and HP's strongest service network in India. The 5300U is still fast enough for student and office workloads, and the 512GB SSD + 8GB RAM config is solid.

Battery is 5.5-6.5 hours of real use — comparable to the Lenovo. If you value HP's brand reliability and IPS display, this is a sensible pick. If raw performance-per-rupee matters more, the Acer or ASUS are better buys.

✓ What works

  • IPS Full HD display
  • HP's service network
  • 512GB SSD
  • Decent build quality

✗ Trade-offs

  • Ryzen 3 5300U is one generation old
  • DDR4 RAM (not DDR5)
  • Often costs more than Acer/ASUS with newer CPU

5. Acer Aspire Lite (Ryzen 3 5300U, 8GB, 256GB SSD)

Usually ₹24,990–₹26,990
CPURyzen 3 5300U (4C/8T)
RAM8GB DDR4
Storage256GB SSD
Display15.6" HD (1366x768)

The Aspire Lite is the budget pick — Acer's lower-cost variant of the Aspire 3. The Ryzen 3 5300U and 8GB RAM are still fast enough for student work. The trade is a 256GB SSD instead of 512GB (still usable, just tighter) and an HD display instead of Full HD. Text looks pixelated on the HD panel during long study sessions.

If your budget is hard-capped under ₹26,000 and you do online classes with light browsing, this is the pick. If you can stretch ₹2,000-₹3,000 more, prefer the Acer Aspire 3 or ASUS VivoBook for the FHD display.

✓ What works

  • Lowest price in this list
  • Ryzen 3 5300U still fast enough
  • 8GB RAM and SSD at this price
  • 5.5-6.5 hour battery

✗ Trade-offs

  • HD display (1366x768) is pixelated
  • Only 256GB SSD
  • Plastic build feels cheaper

The one we recommend skipping

⚠️ Skip

HP 15s with i3 11th gen and 1TB HDD

Usually ₹25,990–₹27,990
CPUi3-1115G4 (2C/4T)
RAM8GB DDR4
Storage1TB HDD
Display15.6" FHD

This HP 15s variant is the most popular under-₹30,000 laptop on Amazon and Flipkart. The 1TB HDD looks great on the spec sheet, and the FHD display is welcome. The 11th-gen i3 is dated (released 2020, two generations behind), but it can still handle student work. So why skip?

The 1TB HDD is the deal-breaker. It boots Windows 11 in 60-90 seconds, takes 10-15 seconds to open Chrome, and copies a 2GB file in 1-2 minutes. An SSD laptop does all of this 3-5x faster. Day after day, the HDD will frustrate you. Every app launch, every restart, every update feels slow.

For ₹1,000-₹2,000 more, the Acer Aspire 3 gives you a current Ryzen 3 7320U, DDR5 RAM and a 512GB SSD. Spend the extra — you will use this laptop for 4-5 years.

The bottom line

For most students and first-time buyers, the Acer Aspire 3 (Ryzen 3 7320U, 8GB DDR5, 512GB SSD) is the right call — current CPU, future-proofed RAM, roomy SSD, and 7-hour battery. If you want an IPS display and sturdier build, the Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 is the runner-up. For tight budgets under ₹26,000, the Acer Aspire Lite works, but expect the HD display to feel dated.

Avoid the HP 15s with the 1TB HDD. The HDD is not worth saving ₹1,000-₹2,000 over an SSD laptop.

Frequently asked questions

Yes, for students, online classes, office work, and browsing. Skip gaming and video editing at this budget — those need ₹50,000+. Look for at least 8GB RAM, an SSD, and a current-gen Intel i3 or AMD Ryzen 3.

Massively. A 256GB SSD boots in 12-15 seconds; a 1TB HDD laptop takes 60-90 seconds. App launch and file copy are 3-5x faster on SSD. Never buy an HDD-only laptop in 2026.

AMD Ryzen 3 wins on multi-core and battery. Intel i3 (12th/13th gen) wins on single-core and software compatibility. For students and office work, both are fine.

6-8 hours of real use is the realistic floor for campus life. Anything below 5 hours means carrying the charger everywhere.

Buy for the storage type, not the size

A 256GB SSD laptop feels faster every day than a 1TB HDD laptop. Pick the SSD model, then add an external drive or cloud storage if you need more space.
